Moving Generator Cluster

Source: R/MGC.R, R/MGC_Function.R, R/MGC_Linear.R, and 4 more
MGC.Rd

Components for building evolving clusters for the DSD_MG data stream generator. Each Moving Generator Cluster (MGC) describes a single cluster: where it is (its center), how large it is and what shape it has (the shape parameters), and how many points it produces (its density). Moving components also describe how these properties change over time.

Usage

MGC(...)

MGC_Function(density, center, parameter, shape = Shape_Gaussian)

MGC_Linear(dimension = 2, keyframelist = NULL, shape = Shape_Gaussian)

keyframe(time, density, center, parameter, reset = FALSE)

add_keyframe(x, time, density, center, parameter, reset = FALSE)

get_keyframes(x)

remove_keyframe(x, time)

MGC_Noise(density, range)

MGC_Random(density, center, parameter, randomness = 1, shape = Shape_Gaussian)

Shape_Gaussian(center, parameter)

Shape_Block(center, parameter)

MGC_Static(density = 1, center, parameter, shape = Shape_Gaussian)

Arguments

...

Further arguments.

density

The relative density of the cluster, i.e., how many points it produces compared to the other components (see Details). For MGC_Function, density is a function of time returning the density. For keyframe() and add_keyframe() it is the density at the keyframe.

center

The center of the cluster as a numeric vector with one value per dimension. For MGC_Function, center is a function of time that returns such a vector. For MGC_Random, this is the starting location of the cluster before it begins to move. For keyframe() and add_keyframe() it is the center at the keyframe.

parameter

Parameters for the shape. For the default shape Shape_Gaussian the parameter is the standard deviation, one per dimension. For Shape_Block, it is the side length. If a single value is specified then it is recycled for all dimensions. For MGC_Function, parameter is a function of time returning the parameter. For keyframe() and add_keyframe() it is the parameter at the keyframe.

shape

A function that creates the shape of the cluster. It is called with the arguments center and parameter and returns a single point. Available functions are Shape_Gaussian (the parameters are standard deviations) and Shape_Block (the parameters are the side lengths of the uniform block). See Details for how to define a new shape.

dimension

Dimensionality of the data stream.

keyframelist

a list of keyframes created with keyframe() to initialize the MGC_Linear object with.

time

The time stamp the keyframe is located at or the time stamp of the keyframe that should be removed. Adding a keyframe at an existing time replaces the existing keyframe with a warning.

reset

Should the trajectory restart at the first keyframe after this keyframe is reached? Only the first keyframe with reset = TRUE is used.

x

An object of class MGC_Linear.

range

The area in which the noise should appear as a matrix with one row per dimension containing the minimum and maximum, e.g., rbind(c(0, 1), c(-1, 1)) for two dimensions.

randomness

The maximum amount the cluster center will move in each dimension during one time step (a uniform step in [-randomness, randomness]).

Value

MGC_Static(), MGC_Noise(), MGC_Linear(), MGC_Function() and MGC_Random() return an MGC object that can be added to a DSD_MG stream. keyframe() returns a keyframe (a list), get_keyframes() returns a data.frame with the keyframes of an MGC_Linear object, and add_keyframe() and remove_keyframe() modify the MGC_Linear object (which is a mutable object, so a stream that contains it is also affected). Shape_Gaussian() and Shape_Block() return a single point as a numeric vector.

Details

A DSD_MG stream is assembled from a list of MGCs. Mixing components with different behavior creates complex evolving streams from simple building blocks. All components of a stream must have the stream's dimensionality.

Static (i.e., not moving) components are:

  • MGC_Static is a stationary cluster with fixed density, center and shape parameters.

  • MGC_Noise produces uniform random noise in the area given by range. It is often used to create individual random outliers.

Moving (evolving) components are:

  • MGC_Linear creates an evolving cluster whose density, center and shape parameters are linearly interpolated between keyframes. Before its first keyframe the component produces no points. After its last keyframe it keeps the attributes of that keyframe, unless a keyframe with reset = TRUE makes the trajectory repeat. keyframe() creates a keyframe (for the keyframelist argument), add_keyframe() and remove_keyframe() modify the keyframes of an existing component, and get_keyframes() returns them as a data.frame.

  • MGC_Function allows users to specify density, center, and parameter as functions of time. This allows arbitrary trajectories.

  • MGC_Random creates a cluster that follows a random walk.

Time and density. Generation in DSD_MG is driven by a generator time that advances as points are drawn. To produce a point, DSD_MG chooses a component with a probability proportional to the current densities of all components and then draws a point from the component's shape. The density is therefore a relative value that determines the chance of choosing a component and, through the total density, how fast time advances: with a total density of 100, approximately 100 points advance the generator by one time unit. Time-dependent arguments (functions and keyframes) refer to this generator time, which starts at 1.

Cluster shapes. The shape of a cluster is given by the shape argument. Available shapes are:

  • Shape_Gaussian (the default) draws from a multivariate normal distribution with independent dimensions. parameter is the standard deviation, one per dimension.

  • Shape_Block draws uniformly from a block (hyper-rectangle) centered at center. parameter gives the side length for each dimension.

If a single value is given as parameter, it is recycled for all dimensions.

New shapes can be defined as a function with arguments center and parameter that returns a single point (a numeric vector with the dimensionality of the stream). Here is the definition of the Gaussian shape as an example:

Shape_Gaussian <- function(center, parameter)
   rnorm(length(center), mean = center, sd = parameter)

See the examples below for a custom ring shape in two dimensions.

See also

DSD_MG for details on how to use an MGC within a DSD.

Author

Matthew Bolanos

Examples

MGC()
#> MGC is an abstract class and cannot be instantiated!
#> 
#> Available subclasses in ‘package:stream’ are:
#> 	MGC_Function,
#> 	MGC_Linear,
#> 	MGC_Noise,
#> 	MGC_Random,
#> 	MGC_Static
#> 
#> To get more information in R Studio, type ‘MGC_’ and hit the Tab key.

### Two static clusters (Gaussian with sd of .1 and a Block with width .4)
###   with added noise
stream <- DSD_MG(dimension = 2,
  MGC_Static(density = .45, center = c(1, 0), parameter= .1, shape = Shape_Gaussian),
  MGC_Static(density = .45, center = c(2, 0), parameter = .4, shape = Shape_Block),
  MGC_Noise( density = .1, range = rbind(c(0, 3), c(-1,1)))
)
stream
#> Moving Data GeneratorClass: DSD_MG, DSD_R, DSD 
#> With 3 clusters in 2 dimensions. Time is 1 

plot(stream)


### Example of several MGC_Randoms which define clusters that randomly move.
stream <- DSD_MG(dimension = 2,
  MGC_Random(density = 100, center=c(1, 0), parameter = .1, randomness = .2),
  MGC_Random(density = 100, center=c(2, 0), parameter = .4,
             shape = Shape_Block, randomness = .2)
)

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
  animate_data(stream, 2500,
               xlim = c(0,3), ylim = c(-1,1),
               horizon = 100)
} # }


### Example of several MGC_Functions

### a block-shaped cluster moving from bottom-left to top-right increasing size
c1 <- MGC_Function(
  density = function(t){ 100 },
  parameter = function(t){ 1 * t },
  center = function(t) c(t, t),
  shape = Shape_Block
  )

### a cluster moving in a circle (default shape is Gaussian)
c2 <- MGC_Function(
  density = function(t){ 25 },
  parameter = function(t){ 5 },
  center= function(t) c(sin(t / 10) * 50 + 50, cos(t / 10) * 50 + 50)
)

stream <- DSD_MG(dimension = 2, c1, c2)

## adding noise after the stream was created
add_cluster(stream, MGC_Noise(density = 10, range = rbind(c(-20, 120), c(-20, 120))))

stream
#> Moving Data GeneratorClass: DSD_MG, DSD_R, DSD 
#> With 3 clusters in 2 dimensions. Time is 1 

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
animate_data(stream, 10000,
             xlim = c(-20, 120), ylim = c(-20, 120),
             horizon = 100)
} # }

### Example of several MGC_Linear: A single cluster splits at time 50 into two.
### Note that c2 starts at time = 50!
stream <- DSD_MG(dimension = 2)
c1 <- MGC_Linear(dimension = 2)
add_keyframe(c1, time = 1,  density = 50, parameter = 5, center = c(0, 0))
add_keyframe(c1, time = 50, density = 50, parameter = 5, center = c(50, 50))
add_keyframe(c1, time = 100,density = 50, parameter = 5, center = c(50, 100))
add_cluster(stream, c1)

c2 <- MGC_Linear(dimension = 2, shape = Shape_Block)
add_keyframe(c2, time = 50, density = 25, parameter = c(10, 10), center = c(50, 50))
add_keyframe(c2, time = 100,density = 25, parameter = c(30, 30), center = c(100, 50))
add_cluster(stream, c2)

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
animate_data(stream, 5000,
             xlim = c(0, 100), ylim = c(0, 100),
             horizon = 100)
} # }

### define your own shape: a ring in two dimensions where `parameter` is the
### radius. Points are spread uniformly around the center with a little noise.
Shape_Ring <- function(center, parameter) {
  angle <- runif(1, 0, 2 * pi)
  center + rnorm(1, mean = parameter[1], sd = 0.02) * c(cos(angle), sin(angle))
}

stream <- DSD_MG(dimension = 2,
  MGC_Static(density = 50, center = c(0.5, 0.5), parameter = 0.3,
    shape = Shape_Ring),
  MGC_Static(density = 25, center = c(0.5, 0.5), parameter = 0.05)
)
plot(stream, n = 500, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1))


### two fixed and a moving cluster
stream <- DSD_MG(dimension = 2,
  MGC_Static(density = 1, parameter = .1, center = c(0, 0)),
  MGC_Static(density = 1, parameter = .1, center = c(1, 1)),
  MGC_Linear(dimension = 2, list(
    keyframe(time = 0,    density = 1, parameter = .1, center = c(0, 0)),
    keyframe(time = 1000, density = 1, parameter = .1, center = c(1, 1)),
    keyframe(time = 2000, density = 1, parameter = .1, center = c(0, 0), reset = TRUE)
  )))

noise <- MGC_Noise(density = .1, range = rbind(c(-.2, 1.2), c(-.2, 1.2)))
add_cluster(stream, noise)

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
animate_data(stream, n = 2000 * 3.1,
             xlim = c(-.2, 1.2), ylim = c(-.2, 1.2),
             horizon = 200)
} # }
